Rank customer pain points by picking pairs: a free MaxDiff alternative

"How much of a problem is this, 1 to 5?" gets you a column of 4s. MaxDiff surveys fix that by making people choose, but the tools cost money. Asking which of two problems is bigger makes the same trade-off, and a few customers' answers give an order.

The starter list

Question: "Which is the bigger problem for you?"

  1. Setup takes too long
  2. Too expensive for what it does
  3. Reports are hard to read
  4. Missing integrations
  5. Slow customer support
  6. Hard to train new staff
  7. Data export is clunky
  8. Mobile app is limited
  9. Too many notifications
  10. Unclear pricing tiers

Why picking pairs works here

  • Send the link to the customers you interview. Each answers on their own phone and sends you back a short result code; paste the codes in to combine them.
  • The "wider" rank range estimates the order for the customers your respondents stand for, not just these people, so you can see how much a handful of answers settles.
  • Nothing about the respondents is collected: no names, emails or accounts. You get only the codes they choose to send.

What it doesn't do: It is built for a handful to a few dozen respondents who paste codes back, not a panel of thousands, and it is not a market-research sample. Write each pain point in the customer's words, or you rank your own framing.

Compared with what you'd use today

MaxDiff modules in paid survey tools, 1 to 5 rating questions in a free form builder, or reading interview notes. Ratings don't force a choice; paid MaxDiff does but costs a subscription. This asks the same kind of forced choice for free.

Under the hood: a Bradley-Terry model refit after every answer, an adaptive question picker, and a stop rule checked against simulated respondents, including ones whose picks are close calls. The method and its measurements.
